short: The largest state in pre-Columbian America, run without money, markets or writing.
full:
Inca tradition dates the empire's expansion to the repulse of a Chanka attack on Cusco around 1438 and the accession of Pachacuti, who reorganised the state and began the conquests his son Tupac Yupanqui carried into Ecuador and Chile. Tawantinsuyu, the Four Parts Together, ran some 4,000 km down the Andes. It was held together by around 40,000 km of road, relay runners, imperial storehouses, resettlement of whole populations, and a tax paid in labour rather than goods, with records kept on knotted khipu cords.

An epidemic that ran ahead of the Europeans, probably smallpox, killed the emperor Huayna Capac and triggered a succession war between Atahualpa and Huascar. Francisco Pizarro landed with fewer than 200 men into that division, seized Atahualpa at Cajamarca in November 1532, took a room filled with gold as ransom and had him executed on 26 July 1533, the usual end date. A neo-Inca state held out at Vilcabamba until 1572.
